messages:
incidents-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and tail latency detected from apac-edge-proxy cluster (apac-prod-edge-1). Error rate spike starting 2034567860. Auto-escalation: paging oncall for incidents channel.

alice (oncall): seen it. paging PD now. attaching first-pass metrics and sample traces.

alice (oncall): quick summary: 5xxs ~8% at peak from edge proxy -> origin 502/504s, tail p99 latency up to 1.6s, increased queueing on proxy pods. Looks region-local (apac) but some cross-region failovers too.

ben: thanks — I'm grabbing logs. /whoami then I'll check provider health (provider-a).

sre_lead: tagging for mitigation options: 1) apply conservative rate limiting per-customer, 2) route a portion of traffic to provider-b, 3) soft brownout: disable non-critical features (image generation, long-context streaming) in apac, 4) scale proxy group if quick capacity available. Prioritize (1)+(2).

jordan: customer-impact check in-progress. CS pulling list of top 25 customers by QPS in apac.

netops: provider-a telemetry shows increased retries and 502s at their egress edge. Provider-b health is green. We can shift traffic at the router layer.

alice (oncall): plan: (A) Add temporary per-key rate limit to throttle high-QPS keys, (B) perform a staged provider reroute -> start with 30% to provider-b for stateless requests, monitor, then increase to 70% if stable. (C) If error rate not trending down in 10m, we'll enable partial brownout for streaming endpoints.

ben: executing (A) now. Command: ```rctl apply --scope=apac-edge-proxy --rule='rate:requests_per_minute=1200' --selector='customer.top=10' --reason='auto-mitigate-2034567890'```

ben: rctl returned: OK. Rule id = r-9f3a. Applied to top-10 customers in apac.

alice (oncall): adding a fast quota deny for heavy backfills: ```policyctl patch quota --cluster apac-prod-edge-1 --max-tokens 50000 --selector 'batch=true'``` — this will block large batch jobs that are noisily retrying.

ops-bot: audit: policy patch queued by alice (oncall) at 2034567925.

jordan: CS list ready. Pushing targeted messages to 6 affected customers (high QPS). Template sent: "We're seeing elevated errors — we're applying temporary rate limits and may route traffic to a fallback provider. We'll follow up with post-incident notes."

netops: starting staged reroute: ```traffic-router shift --from provider-a --to provider-b --cluster apac-prod-edge-1 --percent 30 --mode gradual --window 60s```

netops: shift in progress — controllers report 28% now. No immediate uptick in 5xx from provider-b.

sre_lead: good — observe error rate and latency for 2 minutes. If 5xxs drop by >=50%, continue to 70%. If not, revert and attempt scaling.

alice (oncall): monitoring: 5xx rate moving 8% -> 4.5% within 90s. p99 latency dropping to ~900ms. This is promising.

ben: logs show a subset of proxies still hitting origin timeouts; suspects are older proxy pods with full accept queues. Scaling pods now: ```k scale deployment apac-edge-proxy --replicas=12``` (was 8).

ops-bot: deploy controller acknowledgement: scale request accepted, rolling scale initiated.

matt: quick note — I'm disabling streaming multiplexing on apac region to reduce upstream pressure. This will stop chunked streaming for non-critical routes. Command: ```featureflag disable streaming_mux --env=apac```.

alice (oncall): OK to do brownout? This is a targeted brownout (streaming + image gen) and we've warned CS. Proceed.

matt: done. flags toggled at 2034567990. Observability note: please allow 30s for flags to propagate.

jordan: CS updated customers that may see degraded UX. No major enterprise escalations yet.

sre_lead: next step: continue to increment provider-b to 70% over next 4 minutes if metrics hold. Also keep rate limit in place for top customers until 1 hour post-incident.

netops: increasing shift to 70%: ```traffic-router shift --from provider-a --to provider-b --cluster apac-prod-edge-1 --percent 70 --mode gradual --window 90s```

netops: now at ~68%. Provider-b handling healthy. Core 5xxs dropped to 1.2% and p99 ~420ms.

ben: confirming: scaled proxies are registering and accept queues reduced. No pod OOMs.

alice (oncall): preparing oncall handoff to ben for 1h watch. Handoff notes: "; incident id 2034567890; mitigation: top-customer rate limit r-9f3a applied; batch quota lowered; provider-b routed 70%; streaming mux disabled in apac; proxy scaled to 12 replicas. Monitoring for error regressions and any new customer escalations. Contact: ben -> PD pager or #incidents."

ben: I accept handoff. I'll keep an eye for >=1% rollback threshold on 5xx or new provider-b anomalies.

alice (oncall): leaving channel, ping me if anything unusual. Thanks team.

customer-success: brief from CS: two small customers reported intermittent 502s earlier but now resolved after reroute. Will open follow-up tickets for postmortem if they want credits.

sre_lead: action items captured: (1) follow-up: root cause likely provider-a ingress instability; (2) infra: review proxy accept queue tuning and autoscale policies; (3) product: evaluate feature-brownoutability for future events. Assigning owners in ticketing.

ben: setting post-incident timeline and creating postmortem stub: PRD-2034567890. Estimated wrap-up meeting 2034568500 (≈10m from now).

ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Severity: SEV-2. Recorded mitigations: rate limit r-9f3a, quota patch, provider shift 70%, streaming_mux off, scaled proxies to 12.

alice (oncall): closing paging. Thanks all.

ben: standing by, will follow up with detailed timeline and metrics in the postmortem.

incidents-bot: NOTE: If error rate stays <1.5% for 30m and no regressions, consider rolling back provider shift to normal weights and re-enable streaming with a canary."
